reviews.review: Back4blood is a game I REALLY wanted to be good and like. I love games like this and i adored the Left4Dead series but I can't recommend this to people the way it is. The game is awfully paced, It's balanced around the card system rather than the game mechanics itself. So if you are starting a fresh run its punishing because the game will still balance itself as if you have a full deck you are playing with. RnG will punish you at every turn, Throwing way too many specials at you. Its tough enough because the game wont give you any weapons better than "white" weapons (the lowest quality) and they will throw mutation cards making all the specials and some times the regular zombies super tough to kill. It feels that no matter how skilled at the game no matter how much you try to work with your team. The game will punish you with RnG and thats it. The run is over and nothing you can do about it. It hurts to say but do not buy this game. Its way too overpriced anyway if it was very good id be cautious about recommending it anyway. maybe if they balance the game better it would change my mind. but at the moment, Stay away.

Back 4 Blood has the very difficult task of succeeding Left 4 Dead 2. If you want the answer immediately: It fails. Badly at that. And it's heartbreaking because I was really excited to play a spiritual successor to L4D2, and maybe even see some potential improvements upon the popular classic.

Let's see what it does better than L4D2, because it'll be easy to list:
- Nothing.

So what are the things that I immediately noticed, that suck donkey doink?
- Movement is extremely stiff, no momentum at all. You'll notice it right off the bat.
- Boring story and bland characters.
- Matchmaking takes long for some reason, and puts you in a lobby with only one other person.
- Attachments cannot be removed and are lost if you switch weapons.
- AI is literally retarded.
- No sound cues for when special Ridden appear, with leads to you suddenly dying with no way of preparing for it.
- Normal difficulty (called Veteran) is extremely hard with randoms. I'm up for a challenge but failing a run consistently with different people at the first level is not reasonable. Hard difficulty is the equivalent of the developers taking a dump in your mouth. 
- Card/perk mechanics could be better, but I'd honestly prefer no system at all and keep it simple.
- Cannot change difficulty mid-run, you must restart the entire campaign.

There's still more issues, but this review is already long enough. It's not a game you can just jump-in and have fun right away like L4D2. It could have easily copied L4D2, barely change anything and I'm pretty sure it would've worked well. But instead they tried to kind of set it apart, and it just falls flat on its face. Credit where credit is due, TRS tried to get creative on it. But sometimes it's just best to leave things simple. 

Get it on sale if you really must, but in all honesty, it brings nothing more than L4D2. Maybe even less, since L4D2 has mods and stuff. And wayyyyyy cheaper.

Honestly, this is the first mixed review I'm ever going to give for any game.

First, let's start out with the positives. This game is fun. A great time with friends, with lots of Ridden variety, weapon variety, rewards you for scavenging (which I love) and building decks to suit different builds is enjoyable, and I find addicting sometimes. And truth be told, I enjoy that each act has decent length. Usually much longer than any campaign in L4D could be.

However, despite my praise, I can not ignore the many negatives that surround this game. Let's start out with the most common problems. First, the servers are terrible. Even in co-op, which -- imo, should be local hosted -- the servers are extremely laggy, and can very often cause frustrations, with Ridden not being hit by you, or sometimes even dying, coming back to life, and then dying again, or not dying at all. That happens more often than you might think. The game is WAY too difficult on Veteran and above. Sometimes, it will be a cakewalk if you have a good team, and sometimes, it'll be non-stop special spawning that will never give you a SECOND to breathe. And with the trauma system in play, the never giving you any breaks is only ensuring that you are getting weaker and weaker over time, while the Ridden only get stronger.

There is no counterplay to certain Mutations. As an example, the Bruiser has a weak point on his arm that's always BEHIND it, when it runs at you. Some people may say to just kite it around while your teammates shoot it. What happens when you're indoors and don't have room to do that? What happens if there's 4 Hockers roaming outside at the same time? (Yes, this is VERY common. There's no LIMIT to how many special can be alive at once, it seems.) Point is, the game and level design constantly put you in situations where you can't counterplay any kind of Mutation, with them all being super tanky, and there can be more specials than even the most competent of teams can handle most of the time.

There are a few levels where you're treading through repeat areas, and a lot of people complain about them, but PERSONALLY, they don't bug me, because usually those levels have new areas added to them, to make them somewhat different, but if going through similar areas bugs you, then that's something to point out. In the trailers, they advertised that the card system was in play for you to pre-plan and counter the AI Director's cards, but this was false advertising, as each playthrough is RNG, with no way of being able to tell what the director will throw at you, to throw what COULD be counterplay out the window.

Another gripe of mine, is that ammo is a problem with tanky enemies, and certain weapons are not worth using over others. Personally, I think the SMG's are lacking in power, when you desperately need such to take out the constant spam of Mutations. There is also not many cards in the game currently that help you strengthen yourself with neither SMG's or pistols, so you won't get more value out of them than say AR's or shotguns. But with ammo being a problem, everyone on the team NEEDS to use different weapons to not hog all of the good ammo.

In the current state of the game, it feels very beta still, and they plan on making updates annual! That usually means, if we want any changes, such as balancing (which the game's difficulty DESPERATELY needs) more content, or even FIXES, we have to wait a long time.With that being the case, I see this game probably dying before long, because it STILL has so many more issues I couldn't cover here. And that's a shame, because it's INCREDIBLY fun and has SO much potential to be great.

If you can look past the issues and enjoy challenge, you WILL have fun, and the game is worth it. Maybe not for full price in its current state, but if it goes on sale, I definitely recommend you give it a shot. Good luck if you decide to try it! (You'll need it.)

Well now that content support has ended, I think I can rewrite my review to be about everything in the game. (I do not care that content support has ended, I was hopeful it wouldn't happen but it did and we just have to live with it. Those of you calling TRS money grabbers need to chill, if they really were that, they'd have shut down the servers and told you to ♥♥♥♥ off too.)

Now, first off, yes, I think this game is good. In fact, I think it's better than L4D. Murder me if you must, but that's just my opinion as someone who's played a lot of all three games.

Pricing is, fickle. Personally, I spent $100 dollars, but NOT on the Ultimate Edition. Keep this in mind, it's important. I do think i got my money's worth and then some, and I do think that if you go into the game with an open mind the base $60 price of the game is fine. If you're expecting identical to L4D gameplay, then, wait on a price drop if you're still interested after I tell you that's not what the game is.

Remember when I said I DIDN'T buy the Ultimate Edition? Yeah, that means I permanently locked myself out of the Battle Hardened skin set for the Cleaners. I bought the annual pass separately, and because of owning the base game already, I'm not allowed to buy the Ultimate Edition to get access to those skins. So if you care about those skins, and actually want them, buy Ultimate Edition, otherwise you can't get them at all because there's no upgrade option. Thanks WB!

On to the gameplay, it's quite a lot of fun. The movement feels nice, gunplay is good, the card system is great fun, there's not a lot I dislike about the game, but there are some things. For one, the attachment system wasn't well thought out when it comes to playing with randoms in pubs. You just dropped a legendary attachment by accident? Oh well, the brand new guy who just installed the game saw a shiny yellow object and grabbed it, so it's most likely gone forever now! Trying to swap attachments? That guy that wanted your attachment since the beginning can just yoink it while you're doing so. The attachments are fun to use but their implementation leaves a lot to be desired.

Movement and gunplay are subjective but to me they feel very nice here, and way better than L4D's. The mantle system is a bit finicky at times but is overall a nice addition, ADS is something I could've lived without but it's fine, doesn't slow you down obnoxiously unless you're using heavier weapons like the Barrett M95. This bit of the game is really up to you whether you like it or not, I can't say a lot about it other than "I liked it".

The card system has changed a lot, and had several different major versions. The first, in the alpha was the fully random system. You'd make a deck of 15, and it'd give you a random set of 4 from that deck to choose from at the start of each level. Then, we had the "single draw system" from beta to June of 2022, which was just the previous system, but it was in order of how you assembled your deck. Now we have what's known as "full deck draw" where you just have all 15 of your cards from the start, making it a glorified perk system. Personally, my favorite system was the alpha's random draw system, but the current full deck draw system is fine as well. A lot of people disagree on that, but it just feels nicer to me to actually test my decks immediately, rather than going through 8 levels and only then realizing a change I want to make, and then having to do those 8 levels again to test it once more.

The base campaign overall is fun, I enjoyed it a lot but had some issues with how it was structured, and certain levels I just plain don't like. The Act system is just too long, and it makes it difficult to justify hopping in to just have fun when you'll never really get to have better weapons and items if you only play a couple levels. Yes, you can save runs for later and continue them, but the problem with that is you can't do that when playing public lobbies. The continue system is also entirely unnecessary, as it just hampers the entire experience. You died more than once and want to give that level another go? Too bad, restart from your last checkpont. It's archaic and not fun, there's a good reason most games have removed lives and continues when their previous entries had them.

Certain levels feel very poorly designed and are just a slog to go through. The levels that I hate the MOST are T-5, The Handyman, and The Body Dump. All of them are long, obnoxious, and just not fun for me. You might still find enjoyment out of them, but they were lowpoints for me.

The 3 DLCs were overall great, I enjoyed all of what they added. The 4 extra Cleaners are all great, Act 5 and 6 are both fantastic, the hives are cool despite their obnoxiously high spawn rate causing runs to extend to be several more hours long, and the new weapons and items are quite useful and fun. The only major problem I have is with hives in public lobbies. Yes you can just "choose not to go in" but when you're in a public lobby and EVERYONE wants to go into EVERY SINGLE HIVE it gets tedious having to either go with them despite not wanting to at the time, or just leaving and finding another lobby that will likely be exactly the same.

My obligatory overall rating in a number format? 8/10. Great game, could've been better and hopefully will at least get some bugfix and QoL patches in the future.

First, I'm currently slightly past the halfpoint of the game. I want to finish  the game at least once and if there is a significant change in my opinion, I will obviously update my review.

This game is heavily overpriced for what you currently get. I don't see myself playing through the game a second time, since for me the replay value isn't there and on most of the maps you will have more or less the same objectives. The levels aren't very different to one another and you return to previously visited places very often. 

The card system as a progression is interesting, but I think I would have preferred a skill system. After you finish one act, you lose all weapons and cards you have had from the previous act, since the run is considered finished. Most of the time that was the point where you were starting to get a good build together, which now is gone again and you start from the beginning.

Also you can not remove attachments from your current weapon and add them to a new weapon you found. So most of the time if you find a weapon and it doesn't already have good attachments, you will prefer to keep your current weapon.

A very positive point I would like to highlight is the performance/optimization of the game. I probably haven't played a game on release which ran so smooth in years.

I would recommend it for maybe 25-30 bucks but not at full price.

Stuttery/choppy movement on KB/M. I've figured out the reason - every time you press a movement key (WASD), it jumps in that direct quite a bit very fast, and only after that does it smoothly move you as you continue to hold down the button. So changing directions feel very strange and choppy.

Devs need to address this and it can be done simply by having smoother movement (slower velocity) when you initially press a movement key, possibly combined with a smaller amount of initial movement distance.

Otherwise, this choppiness makes the game feel very clunky and unplayable for me.

Could have been a great game, and could still possibly become one with a lot of balance and content patches. The problem is, though, that the developers seem to either ignore feedback or just actively go against it. Biggest example of this being how players complained about Nightmare difficulty being too hard in the open beta, so naturally they just make it even harder on release and decrease the original 3 continues system down to just 1 continue for some reason???

In addition to this, the community quite unanimously pleaded for a Campaign VS game mode (literally their discord, youtube videos, and Twitch streams were being covered with comments asking for it). Despite this, the devs either made poor excuses for why it couldn't be done or just straight up ignored any comment asking for it regardless of how insanely popular the game mode is. Even if Campaign VS were to be released right now as I'm typing this review, while the game still has a ton of balancing issues, it'd still be FAR more fun and enjoyable than the PVP mode we did end up getting, Swarm Mode.................... 

I don't want to talk about Swarm Mode... 

There are way too many highly questionable design decisions and just straight up flaws i could list here, but I'll leave that to the other negative reviews to list off. Just talking about this game depresses me. And no, not because it's "not l4d". It could have been such a better game on it's own, without needing to be at all like L4D, but as it stands right now, there's barely anything to do in it quite frankly. You grind for cards in coop so you can make a broken deck to either race through or utterly destroy Nightmare Mode with and then you're done. If you think Swarm Mode will keep you entertained... oh lord, good luck to you, buddy. I sincerely wish you the best on that one. 

Basically if this game were like $30 cheaper, I'd say it's worth a try, but it's still very lacking. At it's current price point, with all the very not fun issues it has, no, don't waste your money, don't waste your sanity, just move on. Find something more worth your money and time.

UPDATED REVIEW 05/09/22

 Updates have improved the game and given it MUCH NEEDED balance. Attempt to be left 4 dead 2: 2 was dropped and it feels like they're going heavier down the roguelike path. Which I've been MASSIVELY enjoying.
Side areas with more challenge and TONS of good loot. They apparently added unique legendary weapons. More unique legendary attachments. We're talking UMP that shoots electric bolts at people, mallets that explode when you melee, snipers that mark enemies to take 20% more damage, M4A1 that shoots poison infused bullets that stack a damage over time effect.

Like at first this game just felt like roguelite left 4 dead. After the updates since launch, this game feels more like it's finding its identity. 

The decks are insane, harder to achieve cards are busted, build options are expanded, more variety, more challenge, better balance, I think character stats and passives have been improved as well.

It's all fun. Dont come into this game expecting Left 4 dead. It's a left 4 dead THEMED roguelite. You can make a shotgun deck that makes you a monstorous tank. You can make a glass cannon build that has stacking buffs that melt everything until you get hit. You can make a tank build and absorb damage from allies and just take massive punishment (and there'es a unique LMG that taunts enemies within 30 meters)

You can disable sprinting and aiming down sights to get massive stat boosts for melee. I havent tried this build yet, but I'll be sitting at roughly 60% damage resist, 60% melee damage, like 80% melee attack speed, cleave, power attack, no penalty for hitting special zombies in melee etc.

It gets CRAZY. You just have to suffer a bit at the start of the game. It NEEDS to give you more cards to start off because you'll think the game is super bland before you get crazy cards.
Reminds me a lot of the Outbreak event R6 Siege released in 2018, great game!
